label: Status Hero
title: Status Hero
summary: Use a Status Hero at the top of a result screen to confirm what just happened: a mark, the amount, a title, and one line.
corePrinciple: Say what happened, then the one thing that follows.

anatomy.title: A mark, an amount, two lines
anatomy.description: The media, a mark over the amount, sits on top; the title and the subtitle follow. Everything is centred.

configuration.title: The mark, or your own media
configuration.description: The mark is gold by default: the hero fixes its Icon Capsule to AppearanceBrand Primary, so no brand mode changes it. Set Semantic Intent to System and AppearanceSystem colours it green, orange, or red; pick a matching iconName. renderMedia replaces the mark and the amount with your own content, such as a picture.

We’ll tell you when your bank confirms it.

states.title: Full, or shorter
states.description: The hero has no states: it doesn’t press, load, or animate, and it has no button, so the screen adds the next action. showTitle={false} hides the title, and an empty subtitle hides the subtitle; leaving subtitle out shows the package’s default sentence instead.

sizing.title: As wide as its words
sizing.description: The hero has no width of its own: it centres its content and wraps text only when its host is narrower. With the default copy it is 302 × 269: 8 px of padding, an 81 px mark, 46 px to a 44 px amount, then 12 px to a 24 px title and 12 px to the subtitle. Figma’s is 259 px tall, because its amount and title sit on 36 and 22 px lines.
specimen: ₹50 will be auto-invested daily, stay consistent & stay golden.

content.title: The outcome, then one fact
content.description: Write title as the outcome in a few words, such as Payment successful. Write subtitle as the one fact that follows; a line break in it stays. Give value as the number alone: currency adds the sign, and INR or ₹ both show ₹. Screen readers read the amount once, with its currency.
blocks: The title gives the outcome; the subtitle says where the money went.

inContext.title: The screen after a setup
inContext.description: Start saving swaps the setup screen for the result: the hero confirms it, and Done below leaves. The hero has no button of its own, so the screen adds one.

doDont.title: One result, said plainly
doDont.description: Each pair shows a result people take in at a glance next to one that contradicts or overloads it.

sources.title: Use the public Status Hero contract
sources.description: The guide compares the Figma component with the installed package and its Storybook stories.
blocks: Installed jfs-components is 0.1.78 (27 October build of Biscuit’s main) from the team’s private package repository. Figma’s Status Hero has Title and Subtitle text properties and a title switch, over a nested Icon Capsule and Money Value; the package adds iconName, value, currency, and renderMedia. Its mark is gold where Figma’s is dark grey with a white tick: the hero fixes the capsule’s brand mode, so only Semantic Intent System recolours it. It is 269 px tall where Figma’s is 259, and Storybook’s Without subtitle story still shows the default subtitle (both reported). Screen readers read the amount once, with its currency.
